# Temple Scroll Column 39 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 39 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**39:1** Dig a moat around the temple, outside the outer court wall, to keep people from rushing into My temple unannounced.

**39:2** The moat shall be a hundred cubits wide and very deep.

**39:3** Leave a strip of land seven cubits wide between the moat and the outer court wall, and plant trees there.

**39:4** Build a railing along the moat so no one falls in.

**39:5** No one shall defile My temple by rushing in while still impure.

**39:6** They must treat My temple as holy and stand in awe of My sanctuary — for I live among them.

**39:7** Build public toilets outside the temple city, to the northwest, well away from the city.

**39:8** These shall be roofed shelters built over deep pits into which the waste will fall.

**39:9** They must not be visible from anywhere in the temple city.

**39:10** No one may use them on the Sabbath — they shall be three thousand cubits from the temple city.

**39:11** Set up three separate areas east of the city for people with different types of impurity.

**39:12** One area for those with skin diseases, one for those with bodily discharges, and one for men who have had a seminal emission.

**39:13** None of them may enter the temple city until purification is complete. On the day they are purified, they must wash and be clean.

**39:14** They must bring the required offerings, and the priest shall pronounce them clean.

**39:15** Only then may they enter the temple city — no impure person may be found within it.

**39:16** It is the city of the temple. I, the LORD, have made it holy and placed My name upon it. It shall be holy forever.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column covers three practical features: a defensive moat, public latrines, and quarantine zones. The Sabbath prohibition on using the latrines (placed 3,000 cubits away, beyond walking distance on the Sabbath) reflects the strict Qumran interpretation. The moat adds a physical barrier reinforcing the spiritual boundary.*
